uncited: Unbiased Depth Rendering is a technique for estimating precise depth maps and normal maps from 3D Gaussian Splatting by approximating the underlying surface geometry.
It sets itself apart from weighted average depth methods by flattening 3D Gaussian ellipsoids into planes, allowing depth to be calculated via ray-plane intersections rather than simple accumulation.
This approach aims to reduce depth ambiguity at sharp edges and better reflect actual surface geometry.
*   A set of 3D Gaussians, each defined by mean position $\mu_i$, covariance (implicitly defining orientation/normal $n_i$), and opacity $\alpha_i$.
*   Camera parameters: intrinsic matrix $K$, camera center $T_C$, and world-to-camera rotation matrix $R_c$.
*   Image resolution and pixel coordinates.
*   Normal map $N(p)$ for each pixel $p$.
*   **Gaussian Attributes:** For each Gaussian $i$, store $\mu_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$, normal vector $n_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$ (unit length), opacity $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$.
*   **Camera Matrices:** $K \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$, $R_c \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$, $T_C \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
For each 3D Gaussian $i$, approximate its ellipsoidal shape as a plane.
The normal of this plane is derived from the Gaussian's orientation.
The distance $d_i$ from the camera center to this flattened plane is calculated.
Here, $\mu_i - T_C$ is the vector from the camera center to the Gaussian mean. $R_c^T$ transforms this vector and the normal $n_i$ into the camera coordinate system.
Compute the accumulated normal vector $N(p)$ at each pixel $p$ by alpha-blending the rotated normals of all Gaussians $i \in M$ that project onto the pixel.
*   $R_c n_i$ is the normal vector of the $i$-th Gaussian rotated into the camera coordinate system.
*   $\alpha_i$ is the opacity of the $i$-th Gaussian.
*   $T_i$ is the transmittance up to Gaussian $i$, defined as $T_i = \prod_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - \alpha_j)$.
Compute the accumulated distance $D(p)$ at each pixel $p$ by alpha-blending the distances $d_i$ of the flattened planes.
Convert the accumulated distance and normal information into a standard depth map $D(p)$ (distance along the viewing ray) using ray-plane intersection logic.
